note: Acceptance gates for a candidate snapshot (crawler/qa.py). Edit a value and the next pipeline run re-evaluates the held candidate (its gates.json records a hash of this file + sentinels.json + categories.json). A null threshold means measure-only: the gate is still measured and reported but can never hold a snapshot. Exception: dept_size_tolerance null only disables the page-count comparison; a department that did not finish or kept no items always fails departments_complete. sample_review.required false skips the Claude sample review and publishes on the deterministic gates alone. live_match (2026-10-12): the rate is over the sampled rows Walmart still lists, a live price within live_match_tolerance of the snapshot counts as a match, and rows Walmart no longer lists are reported on their own (live_missing_max null = never holds): a listing that disappeared is not a wrong price, and donors give old stock. 0.9 was set from the first full crawl (five days long: 93.9% within 5% of the rows still listed); raise it as weekly refreshes keep prices fresher. audit_match_min (2026-10-13) applies the same rule to the weekly audit of the published snapshot, so it is never stricter than live_match_min: the audit re-checks the snapshot the gate just passed. null since 2026-10-19: with the fixed monthly cadence (data/schedule.json refresh.fixed_days) prices are up to a month old by design, so the audit measures drift (audit/latest.json, audit/drift.json) and never opens [audit-regression]; set a rate to alert again. sample_review (2026-10-13): sample_size rows are reviewed batch_size at a time and pooled; junk rows are counted from the examples the model lists (never fewer than its stated rate implies); the snapshot is held on systematic junk, when the one-sided `confidence` lower bound of the junk rate is above max_junk_rate (the target), or when the raw rate reaches hard_max_junk_rate. With 600 rows that is 39 or more junk rows; a true 5% snapshot passes about 94% of the time, a true 8% one is held about 93% of the time. new_rows_only / min_new_rows (2026-10-14): the sample is drawn from the rows the last reviewed snapshot (a passed review, not an approval by hand or a grace publish) did not have, because a refresh changes prices, not the rows already judged; fewer than min_new_rows new rows means no review call and the gate passes saying so. unavailable_grace_days (2026-10-14): when the review cannot run at all (no key, a rejected key, no credits, a retired model, an API outage) for this many days while every deterministic gate passes, the candidate publishes without it and the review-* issue stays open; null holds forever instead.

price_sanity.note: Item prices outside [floor, min(cap, over_p99 x the department's 99th percentile)] are withheld: the app values them at an equivalent instead (crawler/process.py). Caps per department name; default when unnamed. Since 2026-10-19 the crawl keeps no consumable listing above consumable_rules.max_price ($150) or durable listing above durable_rules.max_price ($100) in data/categories.json, so these caps only matter below those; a price more than 10x the median of the same kind of item in its category (and of its per-unit price, when it has one) is withheld too (crawler/valuation.py HIGH_FACTOR).
